summary: Say the counting numbers out loud up to at least 29, without needing objects to count.
Count backward out loud from 10 or higher, without any objects to count.
Say which counting number comes next after any number up to 9.
Read and write the numbers 0 to 10; some may come out backward.
Count groups bigger than four, touching each thing once and saying one number for it.
Count out 5 or more things correctly every time someone asks for that many.
Know a number can tell a place in a line, like first or third, as well as how many.
Guess about how many are in a group without counting, even if the guess is sometimes off.
Say which number comes just after or just before a number up to 5.
Know a group gets bigger when some are added and smaller when some are taken away.
Compare more than two things in some way and put them in order, like shortest to tallest.
Use comparing words like longer, shorter, taller, farthest and closest.
Describe a simple repeating pattern in words or with pictures.
Make the same simple pattern with different things, like turning a color pattern into claps.
Copy a longer, harder repeating pattern using the same kind of objects.
Make a harder pattern again with different things or in a different way, like sounds or moves.
Begin to describe what makes a flat or solid shape what it is, such as its sides and corners.
Put shapes together to make new ones and take shapes apart into smaller ones.
Build and take apart shapes and constructions that get more and more complex.
Join shapes together and split them apart to create new shapes.
Spot shapes with matching halves (symmetry) and make some of your own.
Know a piece may need turning or flipping before it fits into a hole or puzzle.
Spot and describe where things are in space more and more accurately.
Draw a simple map of a place, like a room or the playground.
Match a flat map or picture to the real room or space around you.
Say what feature you used to sort or compare things, like color or size.
While sorting, switch to a new feature to sort by and say what it is.
Help the group collect information and put it on a chart or graph.
Sort the information you collect into groups by one or more features.
Collect information on your own and put it on a chart or graph.
Use words like more, fewer and same to compare what a chart or count shows.
Use collected information to answer questions and solve problems.
Talk about, compare and make sense of information the class has collected.
